content: 1. Dolutegravir/lamivudine is approved as a complete two-drug regimen for the treatment of HIV infection in adults and adolescents who have no prior antiretroviral (ARV) treatment history. It is also indicated for replacing the current ARV regimen in patients who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) on a stable ARV regimen, with no history of treatment failure and no known resistance-associated substitutions. The recommended dose is one tablet (dolutegravir 50 mg/lamivudine 300 mg) taken orally once daily. 2. For patients aged 12 years or older and weighing at least 25 kg, dolutegravir/lamivudine is indicated as a complete two-drug regimen for HIV treatment in those with no prior ARV treatment history or to replace a stable ARV regimen in virologically suppressed patients. Safety and efficacy have not been established in patients under 12 years of age. The recommended dose for eligible patients is one tablet (dolutegravir 50 mg/lamivudine 300 mg) taken orally once daily. 3. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir is a complete regimen for HIV treatment and should not be co-administered with other antiretrovirals. Co-administration with lamivudine is contraindicated due to the risk of therapeutic duplication and increased risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 4. Co-administration of emtricitabine-containing products and lamivudine-containing products should be avoided, as this combination results in therapeutic duplication and increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 5. Antiretroviral (ART) medications may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Patients should discontinue ARTs for at least one month before cell mobilization or the expected duration for medication elimination. 6. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of betibeglogene autotemcel. Patients should avoid ARTs for at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 7. Sorbitol-containing solutions decrease the systemic exposure of lamivudine oral solution, as demonstrated in pediatric studies (e.g., the ARROW trial). This results in lower rates of virologic suppression, reduced plasma lamivudine exposure, and increased development of viral resistance compared to children receiving lamivudine tablets. Co-administration with sorbitol should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 8. Tafenoquine inhibits organic cation transporter-2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporters in vitro, which may increase the levels or effects of lamivudine. Co-administration should be avoided, or substrate-related toxicities should be monitored closely, with dosage adjustments considered if necessary. 9. Trilaciclib, an OCT2, MATE1, and MATE-2K inhibitor, may increase the concentration of lamivudine in the kidney or blood, potentially leading to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 10. Lamivudine increases the levels of cabozantinib by inhibiting MRP2 transporters, which may increase cabozantinib toxicity. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 11. Co-administration of lamivudine and ganciclovir increases the risk of hematologic toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 12. Lamivudine increases the levels of erdafitinib by decreasing renal clearance. Alternatives to OCT2 substrates should be considered, or the dose of OCT2 substrates should be reduced based on tolerability. 13. Co-administration of lamivudine and ribavirin increases the risk of lactic acidosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Therapy should be modified, and alternatives should be used if available. 14. Co-administration of lamivudine and zidovudine increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 15. Co-administration of lamivudine and interferon alfa-2b increases the risk of liver decompensation due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 16. Co-administration of lamivudine and orlistat may result in a loss of virological control in HIV-infected patients due to inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption of lamivudine. HIV RNA levels should be monitored frequently, and orlistat should be discontinued if an increased viral load is confirmed. 17. Co-administration of lamivudine and valganciclovir increases the risk of hematologic toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Therapy should be modified, and alternatives should be used if available. 18. Co-administration of lamivudine and isavuconazonium sulfate, an OCT2 inhibitor, may increase the effects or levels of lamivudine. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Co-administration of lamivudine and sulfamethoxazole increases lamivudine levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Co-administration of lamivudine and ublituximab decreases the effects of lamivudine due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 21. Co-administration of lamivudine and efavirenz increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 22. Co-administration of lamivudine and atazanavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 23. Co-administration of lamivudine and ritonavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 24. Co-administration of lamivudine and tenofovir DF increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 25. Co-administration of lamivudine and tipranavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 26. Co-administration of lamivudine and indinavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 27. Co-administration of lamivudine and nevirapine increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 28. Co-administration of lamivudine and fosamprenavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely. 29. Co-administration of lamivudine and trimethoprim increases the effects of lamivudine due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely for potential toxicity. 30. Co-administration of lamivudine and givinostat, a weak OAT2 inhibitor, may increase the levels or effects of lamivudine. Patients should be closely monitored if co-administered with OCT2-sensitive substrates. 31. Co-administration of lamivudine and lovotibeglogene autotemcel may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period for elimination. 32. Co-administration of lamivudine and elivaldogene autotemcel may interfere with stem cell mobilization. ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization medications and until all apheresis cycles are completed.
